# Documentation


- **Getting Started**
- [Introduction](/docs): A declarative framework for LLM training experiments — SFT, RL, and distillation from a single YAML, built so coding agents can launch experiments, learn from them, and train models continuously.
- [Installation](/docs/installation): Get evsys-sdk installed and run your first experiment without a GPU.
- [Quickstart](/docs/quickstart): Train your first model in five minutes — no GPU, no network — then point it at a real backend.
- Examples
  - [SFT — Supervised Fine-Tuning](/docs/examples/sft): A complete, run-it-yourself SFT walkthrough — JSONL data, a transform, the built-in sft algorithm, in-loop validation, and local logging, explained line by line.
  - [RL — Reinforcement Learning](/docs/examples/rl): A complete, run-it-yourself RL walkthrough — tasks with verifiers as the reward, the built-in rl algorithm, rollouts via Harbor, in-loop validation, and local logging.
  - [SDFT — Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning](/docs/examples/sdft): A complete, run-it-yourself SDFT walkthrough — prompts with gold answers, a frozen teacher built from the same model, the built-in sdft algorithm, in-loop validation, and local logging.
- [Putting it all together — Autoresearch!](/docs/autoresearch): How a coding agent like Claude Code writes its own experiments — reads past results, launches a new run on Tinker, scores it, writes a conclusion, and goes again.

- **Concepts**
- Concepts
  - [Architecture](/docs/concepts/architecture): The whole system at a glance — one ExperimentConfig, five layers, eight registries.
  - [Extensibility](/docs/concepts/extensibility): The registry + Config + kind/params pattern — register your own algorithms, verifiers, backends, and more without forking the SDK.
  - Plugins
    - [Backends](/docs/concepts/plugins/backends): The compute plane that materializes a model and hands training resources to the algorithm.
    - [Algorithms](/docs/concepts/plugins/algorithms): The training recipe — SFT, RL, distillation, or any custom loss — that decides what each batch contains.
    - [Agents](/docs/concepts/plugins/agents): The pluggable rollout harness the policy is trained inside, so it learns to use that harness.
    - [Transforms](/docs/concepts/plugins/transforms): Ordered row-rewriters that turn raw dataset rows into the standardized rows your algorithm consumes.
    - [Verifiers](/docs/concepts/plugins/verifiers): Two reward mechanisms — the Verifier class registry and the in-process verifier-fn registry referenced from task data.
    - [Metrics](/docs/concepts/plugins/metrics): Reducers that collapse per-task, per-sample rewards into one benchmark scalar.
    - [Data stores](/docs/concepts/plugins/data-stores): The read/write layer — where the SDK reads inputs from and writes outputs to.
    - [Log stores](/docs/concepts/plugins/log-stores): Where metrics, hyperparameters, and artifact pointers go as training proceeds.
    - [Callbacks](/docs/concepts/plugins/callbacks): Lifecycle + logging hooks fired through the experiment and training loop.
    - [Inference clients](/docs/concepts/plugins/inference): How evaluation and RL query a model to generate text.
  - [Experiments](/docs/concepts/experiments): The organizing unit — a hypothesis, one or more training runs, and an auto-synthesized conclusion.
  - [Data](/docs/concepts/data): Raw sources → ordered transforms → standardized typed rows that carry only data.
  - [Algorithms & Evaluation](/docs/concepts/algorithms): One contract — train(ctx) -> RunResult — plus an optional gradient toolkit and a test/validation firewall.

- **Guides**
- [Cookbook](/docs/cookbook): End-to-end walkthroughs for the most common tasks.

- **Reference**
- [SDK Reference](/docs/reference): The full hand-written reference for configs, CLI, and protocols.
- [Design & Architecture](/docs/design): Layout, protocols, and the rationale behind the SDK.
